clue.text: Perhaps automatic cleaning work in the capital not on — reach out

indicators.note: not here means the word on is left out of the capital's name

parts.note: Washington is the capital of the United States
taken as written

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of reach are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Someone working in the capital is told to stop and reach out instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on' drops ON from WASHINGTON, leaving WASHINGT; 'out' rearranges REACH to HECAR. 'Automatic' is a car with automatic gears, hence 'Perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: An automatic is a kind of car, so cleaning one is a household chore of this name.

clue.text: Museum's quiet spot between two articles

definitions.note: read as 'Museum is', the 's joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: between puts the quiet and spot pieces inside the pair of articles

parts.note: A and AN are the two forms of the indefinite article
SH is the call for quiet
a mole is a spot on the skin

explanation.surface: A museum is described as a quiet place set among some exhibits.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashmolean in Oxford is a famous university museum of art and archaeology.

clue.text: Grasping female in the grass without BBC English?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the grass goes around the accent

parts.note: hay is dried grass
RP, Received Pronunciation, is the accent once standard on the BBC

explanation.surface: A greedy woman is found lying in the grass, lacking a posh accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is used in its old sense of 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpy is a mythical winged monster and, figuratively, a grasping or shrewish woman.

clue.text: As a mole is not available, he's last to cancel

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of he's, ignoring the apostrophe-s as a possessive

parts.note: to void something is to cancel it

explanation.surface: Someone unavailable leaves a man to be the last to call things off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he's last' takes the last letter of 'he', E (the 's is 'is').
explanation.definitionFit: Naevoid is the adjective meaning like a naevus, the medical word for a mole or birthmark.

clue.text: Fought the man off the American Arctic transporter?

indicators.note: off says the man is taken away from the rest

parts.note: taken as written
a sled carries loads over Arctic snow
he stands for a man

explanation.surface: Someone fought to get a man off an American sledge in the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: THE US SLED with HE taken off leaves T-US-SLED.
explanation.definitionFit: To tussle is to fight or scuffle, so the past tense means fought.

clue.text: Drugs head with side is hindrance to a lawyer

parts.note: E is ecstasy, so plural Es are drugs
the top is the head of something
a page is one side of a sheet of paper

explanation.surface: A drug-taking boss with attitude proves an obstacle to someone in law.
explanation.definitionFit: Estoppage, or estoppel, is a legal bar preventing a party from denying an earlier position.

clue.text: Switched central characters of competent English dramatist

indicators.note: the two middle letters of the word for competent change places

parts.note: able means competent

explanation.surface: Someone capable and English has had the main characters in a play swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the middle B and L of ABLE gives ALBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Albee was the American playwright of Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?

clue.text: Regular summer routine of loose night owl women getting one for nothing

indicators.note: loose letters are free to be rearranged
one for nothing means an A goes in where an O was

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
a means one

explanation.surface: Night-owl women who are loose get something for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap one O in NIGHTOWLWOMEN for A ('getting one for nothing'), then rearrange as 'loose' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting the grass is a weekly garden chore through the summer months.

clue.text: An outing with best friend with you taking the lead?

definitions.text: An outing with best friend with you taking the lead?

parts.words: An outing with best friend with you taking the lead?
parts.note: the best friend is a dog, and taking the lead is literally holding its leash on a stroll

explanation.surface: Going out with your closest friend while you take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog is called man's best friend, and you hold its lead on a daily stroll.

clue.text: Not the same thing as an alternative Scottish tourist attraction

parts.note: the other one is the alternative
Loch Ness, home of the fabled monster, draws visitors to Scotland

explanation.surface: Something different is offered as an alternative to a Scottish sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherness is the quality of being different or distinct, not the same.

clue.text: Ace champ (past tense) getting back part of leg

indicators.note: getting back turns the whole run around

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, ace, written AI
to champ is to bite, and bit is its past tense

explanation.surface: A former champion ace gets back his injured leg.
explanation.walkthrough: AI and BIT together, read backwards, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, the larger of the two bones in the lower leg.

clue.text: Chap into home improvement lacking lead ribbing

indicators.note: lacking lead removes the first letter
into puts the chap inside the home improvement

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home improvement
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man gets into DIY but lacks a lead to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: RON in DIY gives DIRONY; dropping its first letter D leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribbing is mocking teasing, much like sarcastic or ironic remarks.

clue.text: A low-down bit of craft has pro locked out

indicators.note: out says the letters of pro locked are out of order

explanation.surface: A professional is locked out of something sneaky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like skill but means a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship, low down in the vessel.

clue.text: Actor's guile exploited in "Guys and Dolls" leads

definitions.note: read as 'Actor is', the 's joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: exploited means worked over, so the letters are rearranged
leads picks the opening letter of each named word

explanation.surface: An actor uses cunning in a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: GUILE plus G and D (initials of Guys and Dolls) are rearranged as 'exploited' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Gielgud was a celebrated English stage and screen actor.

clue.text: Prepares to drive uphill in poor grade snow?

indicators.note: poor letters are badly arranged and need reordering

explanation.surface: A driver gets ready for a climb on a slope covered in poor snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Shifting to a lower gear before a steep climb gives the car more pulling power.

clue.text: Drink workers producing Scandinavian port

parts.note: a dram is a small drink of spirits
men are workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: Workers' drink is brewed in a northern port.
explanation.definitionFit: Drammen is a port city in southern Norway, on the Drammensfjord.

clue.text: City cat put on gold-plated salver

indicators.note: in a down clue the cat is put on top of the rest

parts.note: mog is informal British for a cat

indicators.note: plated says the gold coats the dish all round

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
a salver is a serving dish

explanation.surface: A cat sits on a gold-plated serving tray.
explanation.definitionFit: Mogadishu is the capital city of Somalia.

clue.text: Holbein, artist, rejected Duke of Westminster's reports

parts.note: Hans Holbein was the Tudor court painter

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the artist reads backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: Holbein and another painter turn down a duke.
explanation.definitionFit: Hansard is the official verbatim record of debates in the Westminster Parliament.

clue.text: A welcome from this put-upon type?

definitions.meaning: a mat at the front step often bears a WELCOME message

explanation.definitionFit: The mat at a front step greets visitors and gets trodden on, like a meek person.

clue.text: Cologne's good stuck on Devon resort's pot

indicators.note: stuck on means the German word is added after the resort

parts.note: Beer is a seaside village in Devon, in south-west England
gut is German for good, as spoken in Cologne

explanation.surface: A German good is attached to a seaside pottery in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot or pot belly is a paunch, like one built by drinking ale.

clue.text: Horse and one time weapon

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse
taken as written

explanation.surface: A horse and a single moment of fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A bayonet is a blade fixed to a rifle, used as a stabbing weapon.

clue.text: Nothing's on the level for an American romance

parts.note: love is a score of nothing in tennis; the 's is 'is'
in American spelling, a floor of a building is a story

explanation.surface: Nothing is fair for an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link; the British spelling would have an extra E.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale of romantic love, such as a Mills and Boon novel, is a romance.

clue.text: Nothing against sweetheart getting end away, overturning car

indicators.note: overturning in a down clue turns the run upside down

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
V is short for versus, against

indicators.note: getting end away removes the last letter of the sweetheart word

parts.note: love is a term for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: With a sweetheart gone, nothing stops a car from overturning.
explanation.walkthrough: O + V + LOV makes OVLOV, then 'overturning' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Volvo is a Swedish make of car.

clue.text: Game not initially before the watershed

indicators.note: not initially drops the first letter

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A game is played before the evening TV watershed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watershed' looks like the 9pm TV cutoff; it is a crest dividing rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A watershed is high ground dividing two river basins, a ridge of land.

clue.text: Upset composure of large abandoned freshwater fish

indicators.note: abandoned says the large letter is left out

parts.note: to ruffle someone is to upset their composure

explanation.surface: A fish loses its composure when abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruffe is a small freshwater fish of the perch family.

clue.text: Ewe in loch: OK but oddly lacking radio compliance

indicators.note: oddly lacking removes the odd-placed letters, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A sheep in a Scottish lake is fine but a bit strange.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio voice procedure, the word means 'will comply' with an instruction.

clue.text: Show ring declaration

parts.note: to manifest is to show
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A show ring makes an announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's published statement of policy is a public declaration of aims.

clue.text: Having intention of getting trendy in Bath — possible reward for 1,8 or 9?

parts.note: going to means intending to

indicators.note: in puts the trendy word inside the bath

parts.note: a tub is a bath
hep is old slang for trendy

explanation.surface: Someone intends to be trendy in Bath, rewarding household chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link. 'Bath' looks like the English city but is a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink at the local is a natural treat after car washing, mowing or a dog walk.
